fix: 'glaucous' means a waxy bloom on the surface, not a green hue; map it to PATO glaucous and keep the 'somewhat' qualifier, and don't use it as a colour value.
reason: The basal leaves are said to be somewhat glaucous, which means covered with a whitish waxy bloom. That is a surface quality, not the colour green.
'Shrubs or small trees' gives two habit alternatives for the whole plant: frutescent and arborescent.
Calyx lobes are sepals here, and 'linear-elliptic' is rightly read as a shape between linear and elliptic.

fix: 'rounded/emarginate at each end' (or 'at both ends') names the apex and the base of the part; make the bearer the apex and the base, not the whole part.
reason: The shapes are said of both ends of the leaflet, not of the leaflet outline. Emarginate in particular only applies to an end.
The underside of the leaf blade is densely tomentose, and the place word 'abaxially' rightly moves the bearer to the lower surface. Density and colour are left out, but nothing stated is false.
'Inflorescence many-flowered' means flowers are present in many in the inflorescence, with the inflorescence as the whole.
'Elliptic to oblong' is a range of leaf-blade shapes; the extra 'or ovate-oblong' is left out but nothing stated is false.
The legume becomes stramineous (straw-coloured, pale yellow) at maturity. Yellow with the 'mature' context matches.
'Involucres numerous' means involucres present in many.
'Capsules ... à 5 valves' means 5 valves per capsule, and the capsule is the whole.

target: density range sparsely to densely; alternatives puberulous | hispidulous | pilosulous
fix: In 'sparsely to densely X, Y, or Z', 'sparsely to densely' is a density range over all the hair types; don't attach 'densely' to the first type alone, and keep every listed alternative.
reason: The relation keeps only 'densely puberulent' and hispidulous. It loses the sparse end of the density range and drops 'pilosulous'.

fix: In a split count like '2 anthers large, 5 medium, 3 small', each number counts a subset picked out by the adjective that follows; keep that adjective as the state, or record only the total from 'Stamens 10'.
reason: The flower has 10 anthers. Only 2 of them are large, so 'anther amount 2' is false without the 'large' qualifier.
The blades of the basal leaves are 10–40 mm long, which matches the bearer, the number and the 'basal' context.

target: leaf, position basal + proximal cauline (FLOPO_0991002 and proximal)
fix: When a series word ('basal and proximal cauline leaves') limits the leaves, keep it as a position context; the median and distal leaves are described separately as still present.
reason: Only the basal and proximal cauline leaves fall by anthesis; the median and distal leaves stay. 'Leaves deciduous at anthesis' with no position is false.
Seeds 1–4 per fruit, read as a count.

fix: In 'median filament pairs ..., not dilated basally' the subject is the filament; keep it as the bearer rather than falling back to stamen, and keep 'basally' as the place on the part.
reason: The flora says the filaments, not the whole stamens, are not widened at their base.
Peduncle 0.2–1.5 cm long.
The bracts under the flower heads are longer than (surpass) the heads, and the comparison is aimed at the capitula.
3 or 4 lateral veins on each side of the midrib, with the 'each side' position kept.

fix: 'Cleistogamous flowers with ... sepals' limits every measure after it to cleistogamous flowers; keep that flower type as the whole or state, especially when the open (chasmogamous) flowers are 'not seen'.
reason: The 5–6 mm sepal length is given only for cleistogamous flowers. The open flowers were not seen, so a general sepal length says more than the flora does.
The basal leaves are petiolate, and the 'basal' context is kept.
The fern stipe is ± rough. PO 'stalk' has 'stipe' as a synonym, and the 'approximately' qualifier is kept.
The staminate (male) spike is linear, and the 'male' state is kept.
Petals white.
Flowers solitary or paired, read as alternatives.
The leaflet blades are 2–6 cm long.

fix: In paired place words like 'proximally thickened, distally appressed', keep the place word as the position on the part; only the distal part of the scale lies flat.
reason: The cup scales are thickened near the base and lie flat only near the tip. Calling the whole scale appressed leaves out that limit.
The pinna (leaflet) is glabrous on its underside, and the bearer is rightly moved to the lower surface.
Blade ovate, elliptic or almost orbicular, read as three alternatives. 'Almost' is not kept, but this is minor.
The ovary is 4-locular, read as 4 locules with the ovary as the whole.
